style: Style: an original illustration in the manner of a 19th-century newspaper steel engraving, hand-tinted: fine black cross-hatched ink lines, a few muted watercolour tints (navy, sepia, dull red, ivory), on warm aged paper with soft foxing. Head-and-shoulders bust, three-quarter view, centred, dignified. Plain aged-paper background fading to the edges, no scenery. Historically plausible dress for the 1860s. Not photorealistic, not a photograph, not anime. No text, no letters, no captions, no signature, no border.

items.seward: William H. Seward, United States Secretary of State, at about 65 in 1867: thin, slightly hunched man with a large hooked nose, shaggy grey eyebrows, thinning untidy grey hair, clean-shaven, wry knowing expression; dark frock coat, high white collar and a loose black cravat.
items.stoeckl: Eduard de Stoeckl, the Russian minister to the United States in 1867, at about 60: a stout diplomat with a full grey beard and moustache, receding hair, calm shrewd eyes; dark diplomatic coat with a small decoration on the lapel.
items.alexander2: Tsar Alexander II of Russia in the 1860s, at about 49: tall, balding man with large dark side-whiskers joined to a thick moustache, clean chin, serious eyes; dark green Russian imperial military tunic with gold epaulettes and a sash with a star.
